title: NVBit Unsupported Memory Path Exclusion
description: Per-(kernel, op-class, instruction-pc) sidecar emitted by the NVBit tracer when it encounters a memory operation whose class the tracer cannot represent (TMA, async_copy, cluster_dsmem, atomic, texture, surface). The sidecar is the contract that lets downstream consumers (sector stream generator, HRD profiler) treat these instances as a typed exclusion rather than silently dropping them or misclassifying them into MEMORY_OP_CLASS_GLOBAL. The plan's AC4 acceptance criteria require this typed exclusion path; this schema is the offline-checkable surface.

schema_version.description: Sidecar schema major version. Pinned to 1; a deliberate schema bump must update both this constant and consumers in lockstep. A different value is a contract violation, not a configuration.

kernel_unique_id.description: Tracer-assigned unique id for the kernel function whose instruction was excluded. Matches `instruction.function_unique_id` and `kernel.function_unique_id` in the trace proto.

device.description: Compute capability tag of the device that produced the trace (e.g. `sm_86`, `sm_120`).

slug.description: Kernel slug from the workload roster (e.g. `gemm_hmma_bf16_sm80`).

path_resolved.description: True when the classifier recognized the opcode and assigned it a memory class (e.g., LDT → kTmem) but the producer still routed it through this typed-exclusion sidecar because the downstream consumer cannot fully model the access (the address-space allocator does not track tensor-memory backing, for example). False or absent means the opcode was genuinely unknown to the classifier (kUnspecified path). Downstream consumers can use this field to distinguish 'opcode recognized + classified but unsupported by allocator' from 'opcode unknown to classifier'; the first case is a known design boundary (TMEM-routed accesses fall here for now), the second is a producer-side classifier coverage gap. Additive OPTIONAL field per the CLAUDE.md wire-extension policy: legacy sidecars omit the field, downstream readers MUST treat absence as 'false / unknown'.

excluded_op_class.description: Memory operation class the tracer skipped. Uppercase string form of the `MemoryOpClass` enum in `instruction.proto`. The 10 named classes correspond directly to the enum (the original 9 plus `TMEM` for Blackwell tensor-memory accesses via the `tcgen05.{ld,st}` family, mnemonics `LDT`/`STT`); `UNSPECIFIED` is the sentinel for STANDARD_MEM opcodes the classifier could not match against any known prefix (e.g., a future SASS opcode for a new memory hierarchy). Producer-side typed exclusion routes those through this sidecar with `excluded_op_class=UNSPECIFIED` so the validator does not reject them as `memory_op_class_missing_on_memory_instruction`.

instruction_pc.description: Virtual program counter of the static instruction. Matches `instruction.vpc` (or, for legacy emitters, `instruction.pc`).

count.description: Number of distinct dynamic instruction-instances of this static PC that the tracer skipped because the op-class is unsupported. Aggregated per (kernel, instruction_pc) so the sidecar does not blow up on hot loops.

typed_reason.description: Pinned to `unsupported_memory_path`. A different value is a contract violation.
